NEITHER (a) NOR (b) — ship (c): register the trigger path as ONE new named strategy with its own pool, priority slot and virgin-day clock; leave the six incumbents' entry path byte-identical.

Why (a) fails — verified, not argued. Against that, _PRICEY_CANDS — already a trigger-identity pool built from the same filter family (:1828-1850) — has an observed conversion of 1 fill in ~76 (confirmed in reports/research/capture_ratio_2026-09-09.md at origin/main f81fb20f). Trigger-only restarts six 8-day clocks onto a path measured at ~1.3% conversion. That is not "cleanest evidence, costs throughput"; it is zero evidence.

Why (b) fails — four counts, all verified. (i) NO READER: scripts/sunday_boundary.py:325-336 buckets solely on `probe_strategy`; `occ_source` is written at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1202/1207/1209/1218/1317 and read by exactly two assertions in scripts/regime_drill.py:80,99 — nothing in the scorer. (ii) NO MULTIPLICITY CONTROL: six strategies x two streams = twelve draws at a fixed `t >= 1.8` one-sided bar, re-evaluated weekly against one shared control (sunday_boundary.py:393-400); no correction exists in the file. (iii) ENDOGENOUS ASSIGNMENT: stream membership is decided by whether the live repricing gate passes (:1349) — a liquidity filter — so the trigger stream is a liquidity-selected subsample and the synth stream its complement; neither estimates the strategy. A code-only edit writes neither, so §5's "their virgin-day evidence restarts" is decorative — pre-change synthesized days keep counting into the same t-test.

Why (c) works: one name = one stream = one clock, so the laundering surface disappears without needing an occ_source reader in the court (the strategy name IS the tag); the incumbents keep their entry path and their accrued days, so no clock restarts and no throughput is spent; and the trigger path's low fill rate becomes a measured fact about that strategy rather than a starvation of six. Note MOT coverage for this is nil today — v11_mot_harness.py contains no reference to trigger_contract, _PROBE_CONTRACT, occ_source or band_lo, so the design's "the existing guards still fire on the trigger path" is unbacked; every fixture is new work.

THE AFFORDABLE SLICE IS BIMODAL, NOT ONE INSTRUMENT — I reproduced the entry lens's geometry and it is right on the numbers but wrong on the mechanism, which changes the fix. On the same three snapshots: survivors n=18 median moneyness +10.51% OTM, median DTE 45, median ask/underlying 2.41%; dropped n=91 median +2.04% OTM, median DTE 45, median ask/underlying 5.65% — matching the lens. But the survivor detail shows two disjoint populations, not one shifted one: six survivors sit at +0.13% to +1.59% OTM on 9-16 DTE (QQQ, GLD, INTC, QQQ, SPY, AAPL — near-ATM, cheap because short-dated), and a tail sits at +12% to +90% OTM on 45-227 DTE (AMZN, GOOGL x3, NOK x2, AA, IREN — cheap because miles out). The medians coincide at DTE 45 only because the two modes cancel. So the lens's claim 'not a nearer expiry — a strike six times further OTM on the same clock' is WRONG; it is both, in two modes. Consequence for the fix: a single re-derived ask<=$10 cell is not enough, because it averages a ~0.5-delta 10-DTE ETF call with a ~0.10-delta 227-DTE small-cap lottery ticket. The exit grid makes this fatal — probe_tuner.py:32-33 and :133-135 fitted -50/+50/0.20 and -70/+80/0.30 on the unfiltered cohort, and a -50% option move means a completely different underlying move in each mode. Publish the slice split by mode (DTE band x moneyness band), not as one number.

MAKE THE BAND ONE CONSTANT AND ENFORCE THE CAP DIRECTLY — there are currently THREE ceilings for one constraint and the cap is held up by coincidence. Pool admits price 4.00 < pc <= 9.00 (:1828); repricing gate admits ask 4.0 <= _la <= 9.9 (:1349); the design proposes ask <= $10 (doc:24). I verified the arithmetic at :1354 `round(round(_la*1.01*20)/20, 2)`: ask 9.90 -> limit 10.00 -> notional exactly $1,000.00 (ZERO headroom vs NORTH_STAR.md:38); ask 9.95 -> $1,005 BREACH; ask 10.00 -> $1,010 BREACH. So implementing the doc's `ask <= $10` and aligning the gate to it — the obvious consistency edit — silently breaches the per-trade cap on six strategies. Nothing catches it: route_to_alpaca_paper (:1429) and _order_payload (:511-518) submit whatever limit_price the leg carries, and alloc_usd records LEG_BUDGET (:454, :1435), not actual spend. Required: derive band_hi from the cap (floor_to_nickel(CAP/100/1.01) = 9.90), have pool, leg and gate all read one module-level constant pair, stamp band_lo explicitly in build_legs and DELETE the 4.0 default so an unstamped leg is a hard error, add an unconditional pre-submit assertion `contracts * limit_price * 100 <= 1000` that skips-with-reason rather than routing, and stamp notional_usd on the leg. (I checked and am dismissing one adjacent concern: the pool bands on `price` while the gate bands on `ask`, but only 2 of 298 in-band alerts had ask > 9.9 — 1%, immaterial.)

CLOSE THE SUBMITTED-BUT-UNLOGGED WINDOW BEFORE ADDING SIX MORE CALLERS. enter_proactive_set routes at :1429, then calls _notify at :1441, then _append_log at :1443 — and _append_log deliberately RAISES when the log exists but will not parse (:1470-1476, the fail-closed 2026-08-25 fix). Separately, the occ guard's stated invariant is 'one record per contract, EVER' (:1359-1362) but it scans only status == 'OPEN' plus broker positions (:1366-1371) — once a record closes the same occ is buyable again, which on a 14-row one-per-ticker pool means a popular monthly contract gets re-bought under a different strategy label and two 'independent' streams contain the same instrument.

INSTRUMENT THE REPRICING GATE FOR TWO WEEKS BEFORE TRUSTING ANY CAPTURE NUMBER. The gate at :1349 fail-closes unless the LIVE ask is inside band — so a candidate admitted at an alert ask of $8.50 and repriced to $10.20 is REJECTED, i.e. the engine discards precisely the names where the post-print move it is betting on has already begun; symmetrically a $4.20 that decayed to $3.80 dies on the floor. The archive has no analogue: its entry is a post-print bar close (probe_tuner.py:128) and it books those run-ups in full. In a cohort this skewed the right tail IS the mean, so this will read as 'the edge didn't survive contact' when the real cause is that the engine refused the winners. Log every fail-closed skip with alert ask, live ask and reason, publish the drift distribution of rejects, and if rejects are systematically higher than their alert ask, the comparator must be censored identically. findings.title: Live repricing floor is hardcoded $4.00 for any leg that doesn't opt out — a $0.30-$10 _TRIG_CANDS pool loses everything under $4 at the gate, after the attempt is already spent, and the survivors are the same pricey slice the fix was meant to escape
findings.attack: The trigger leg built in build_legs carries no band_lo key (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:450-455), so the repricing block falls back to _blo = 4.0 (1347) and fail-closes on `_blo <= _la <= 9.9` (1349). That default was written when the ONLY consumer was _PRICEY_CANDS, whose scan filter is `4.00 < pc <= 9.00` (1828) — the constant and the pool agreed. The design doc's _TRIG_CANDS drops the $4 floor entirely (doc line 24: premium 50k-1M, aggressor, spread<=2%, DTE>=7, ask<=$10). Flow is overwhelmingly cheap: every candidate whose live ask reprices under $4.00 returns `trigger_contract fail-closed` (1350-1352) even though it passed every pool filter and every hypothesis filter. Six strategies now spend the 10-attempt budget (2483, 2506) discovering this one ticker at a time, and the skip reason does not map to any engine_skips code (_skip_code:1447-1464 has no trigger branch), so the discovery is never propagated (2548) — each of the six re-pays for the same dead row. Net effect: the live cohort silently collapses back to $4.00-$9.90, while the doc's comparator (fix #4) is re-derived on ask<=$10. The comparator and the live book disagree in exactly the direction the whole project is trying to fix. Two more guards decay the same way because the trigger row shape differs from the aggregate row shape: (a) the free hopeless-check reads `tight_spread_pct` (2515), which aggx rows never set (1846-1850) while agg rows do (1854, 1864) — `.get(...,0)` returns 0, so the throughput protection added 2026-09-09 for precisely this attempt-budget problem is dead on the trigger pool; (b) the afford_fallback reads `afford_call`/`afford_put` (1300-1303), set only on agg rows (1878-1880) and never on aggx rows, so on the trigger path the fallback is structurally unreachable. That is currently harmless only because contracts=1 (453) clears min_ct=1 (fade_book_spec.json:33). Flip min_contracts to 2 and the affordability gate at 1294 fires, the fallback cannot catch it (1319), and EVERY trigger fill for all six strategies dies as `premium too rich` with no alarm — a single-config fuse under the entire fix.

findings.title: The trigger branch hardcodes LONG_CALL, so moving the two regime-agnostic both-sides strategies onto it makes them calls-only live while their archive cells are both-sided — the fix injects a fresh instrument mismatch into the frozen secondary control
findings.attack: build_legs' trigger branch returns exactly one leg, `{"bullish_call": {..., "structure": "LONG_CALL"}}` (450-455), unconditionally — it never reaches the regime router at 507. That is correct for the four calls-only probes in _CALLS_ONLY (2470-2471). But the doc routes WINNER_PROFILE and WINNER_PROFILE_X onto the same path (doc line 27), and both are deliberately excluded from _CALLS_ONLY. WINNER_PROFILE is documented as the frozen owner control, "Regime-agnostic, both sides", derived from ALL 25,597 labeled trades (2413-2423); WINNER_PROFILE_X's filter is a bare premium threshold with no side term (2424). Today they draw _FULL_CANDS (2500), which is built from `agg` and carries flow_type call OR put (1888). _TRIG_CANDS is calls-only by construction (doc line 22; aggx admits only `type == "call"`, :1828). So after the change these two strategies buy calls in every regime, including BEARISH tape, while the court judges them against a both-sides cohort. That is the same defect as `alpaca_resolved` vs the printed contract — same class, opposite direction — and it lands on the strategy whose entire job is to be the stable control. A hostile room reads it as: the mismatch fix moved the mismatch rather than removing it, and did so silently, because nothing in the record distinguishes 'call because the hypothesis says call' from 'call because the pool only had calls'. Worse, the record's regime field still reports the classified regime (1271, 1430-1434) while the leg is always a call, so the archive re-derivation cannot even reconstruct the constraint after the fact.

findings.title: The $1,000 per-trade cap is enforced by nothing but two coincident literals (9.9 and the nickel round); the doc's `ask <= $10` pool filter breaks it, and no assertion anywhere would catch the breach
findings.attack: On the trigger path sizing is fixed at contracts=1 (453, and re-forced at 1355) and the limit is `round(round(ask * 1.01 * 20) / 20, 2)` (1354). The only thing holding notional under NORTH_STAR v1.7's $1,000 is the band ceiling `_la <= 9.9` at :1349 — the inline comment at :1354 admits the dependency ("caps at $10.00 = the $1k budget"). At ask 9.90 the limit is 10.00 and notional is exactly $1,000.00 — zero headroom. The design doc specifies the pool filter as `ask <= $10` (doc line 24). Anyone implementing that and aligning the repricing band to match (the obvious consistency edit — the current mismatch between pool 4.00-9.00 and band 4.0-9.9 already looks like an oversight) produces: ask 10.00 -> 10.00 * 1.01 = 10.10 -> nickel round 10.10 -> $1,010 per contract, over cap, on six strategies, with no error. Nothing on the entry path asserts the cap: route_to_alpaca_paper (1429) and _order_payload (511-518) submit whatever limit_price the leg carries; `alloc_usd` is recorded as LEG_BUDGET (454, 1435) which is the probe size_usd (2448), not the actual spend, so the record itself would not show the breach either. The same arithmetic exists unguarded in the afford_fallback (1314). A live-money cap that survives only because two magic numbers happen to be 9.9 and 1.01 is not a cap.

findings.fix: Derive the band ceiling from the cap instead of hardcoding it: `band_hi = floor_to_nickel(CAP / 100 / 1.01)` and let the pool filter read the same constant, so `ask <= $10` in the doc cannot silently become $1,010 in the book. Then add an unconditional pre-submit assertion in enter_proactive_set — `contracts * limit_price * 100 <= PER_TRADE_CAP` for every leg, skip-with-reason on breach, never route — and stamp `notional_usd` on each leg so the record shows real spend rather than budget. Cover it in the MOT with an ask-at-the-ceiling fixture.

findings.title: Six strategies onto one per-ticker-deduped, premium-sorted, 14-row pool: two of the filters become tautologies, two thresholds silently change units, the occ guard starves whoever rotates second, and the strategies stop being independent evidence streams
findings.attack: aggx keeps ONE contract per ticker — the single highest-total_premium alert (1844-1850) — and _PRICEY_CANDS truncates to the top 14 by premium (1903). Every strategy scans that same list from index 0 (2505). On a calls-only pool where every row has flow_type == "call" (1846), FOLLOW_CALLS' filter `flow_type == "call"` (2430) is a tautology: it takes row 0, always. CONSENSUS_CALLS adds only `not _shape(md, c)` (2441), and WINNER_PROFILE_X adds `total_premium > 100000` against a pool already banded 50k-400k and sorted descending (1841, 1903) — near-tautological at the head. So four of the six converge on the same contract, and which one gets it is decided by the day-of-month+hour rotation seed (2460), not by hypothesis. The loser does not merely miss out: once the winner's record is appended (1443) the occ guard rejects the same occ (1359-1379) and the ticker guard rejects it via _open_tk (2509, 2560), so the second strategy's skip is manufactured by rotation position. Over weeks each strategy's day-mean is computed on a sample systematically thinned by its rotation slot, and the courts compare those day-means as if independent when they are drawing the same instruments on the same days. The threshold re-scaling is a separate silent error: WINNER_PROFILE's 73200 and WINNER_PROFILE_X's 100000 (2413, 2424) are read today against _FULL_CANDS, where total_premium is the day's call_prem+put_prem AGGREGATED across every alert for that ticker (1883-1889), banded 50k-1M (1906). On aggx, total_premium is a SINGLE alert's premium (1829), banded 50k-400k (1841). The same constant, a different quantity, with a ceiling the archive cell never had. And the comparator does not close this: scripts/capture_ratio.py:35 scores FOLLOW_CALLS against `side == "C"` over the whole corpus — no premium band, no top-14 truncation, no one-per-ticker dedupe, no ask cap — and WINNER_PROFILE/WINNER_PROFILE_X have no MAP entry at all (capture_ratio.py:33-46), so the two strategies the doc is moving have no capture measurement to move. Doc fix #4 adds only the ask<=$10 slice and leaves the other four selection differences in place. Related clock defect: if _TRIG_CANDS is built by widening aggx to the doc's 50k-1M / ask<=$10 (from 50k-400k / $4-9), that is an entry-path change for DIP_CONF_MILD and BULL_DIP_X too — the doc restarts clocks for six strategies (doc lines 27, 40-41) and names neither.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1844-1850 (one contract per ticker, max premium); :1903 (top-14 by premium); :2505,:2430,:2441 (tautological head-taking); :1846 (every row flow_type call); :2413,:2424 vs :1883-1889,:1906 vs :1829,:1841 (threshold units + band change); :2460 (rotation seed decides the winner); :1359-1379,:2509,:2560 (occ/ticker guards convert rotation order into evidence starvation); scripts/capture_ratio.py:35 (archive predicate has no premium band or truncation), :33-46 (no WINNER_PROFILE/_X row); reports/instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:27,39,40-41
findings.fix: Three changes before any of this ships. (1) Stop deduping by ticker for a contract-identity pool — key _TRIG_CANDS by occ and keep the top N contracts, so six strategies are not fighting over 14 rows; and give each strategy a rotated offset into the pool rather than all starting at index 0, so head-taking is not a function of rotation slot. (2) Re-derive 73200 and 100000 against the per-alert quantity the trigger pool actually carries, or switch the pool row to expose both `alert_premium` and `ticker_premium` and have each filter name which one it means — a threshold whose units changed is a new strategy, not the same one. (3) Extend capture_ratio.py's MAP predicates to include the full live selection (premium band, ask cap, dedupe/truncation) and add WINNER_PROFILE/WINNER_PROFILE_X rows, or the doc's 'comparator honesty' item is unmeasurable. Add DIP_CONF_MILD and BULL_DIP_X to the clock-restart list, or build _TRIG_CANDS as a separate pool and leave aggx byte-identical.

findings.title: The submitted-but-unlogged window is swallowed by a bare `except: continue` in the probe loop, and the trigger path triples both the odds of hitting it and the cost when it hits
findings.attack: enter_proactive_set routes the order at :1429 and only then builds and appends the record at :1430-1443. _append_log deliberately raises if the log file exists but will not parse (:1470-1476, the fail-closed 2026-08-25 fix) — correct in isolation, but the probe loop catches every exception from enter_proactive_set with a bare `except Exception: continue` (:2539-2540) that prints nothing, and the outer probe handler prints only a type name (:2571-2572). So a corrupt log, a _notify path fault, or any other post-submit raise yields a live paper position with no record: no leg_exits tracking (:998), no backstop, invisible to the occ guard's OPEN scan (:1365-1369) and to _open_tk (:2345), and permanently outside the one-record-per-contract invariant. Six strategies on the trigger path make this materially likelier because each trigger attempt adds its own synchronous quote call with timeout=15 (:1338-1346) on top of the sensor sweep, against a 10-attempt budget (:2483) inside a job with `timeout-minutes: 8` (.github/workflows/v10_lab.yml:33) — the same latency envelope whose overrun is already documented in-code as the cause of the 17:40Z cancellation churn (:2472-2479). A GitHub hard-timeout landing between :1429 and :1443 produces exactly the same untracked position, with no exception to catch at all. Separately, the occ guard's stated invariant is 'one record per contract, ever' (:1359-1362) but it only scans records with status == "OPEN" (:1366) plus current broker positions (:1370-1371); once a record closes the same occ is buyable again. That gap is tolerable with one trigger strategy and a rotating pool; with six strategies pulling from a 14-row per-ticker pool where a popular monthly contract reprints for days, the same instrument will be re-bought under a different strategy label and two strategies' 'independent' evidence will contain the same contract.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1429 (submit) vs :1443 (append) — the unprotected window; :1470-1476 (_append_log raises by design); :2539-2540 (bare except, silent continue); :2571-2572 (outer handler prints a type name only); :1338-1346 (per-trigger 15s quote call); :2483 (10-attempt budget); :2472-2479 (documented cycle-time overrun); .github/workflows/v10_lab.yml:33 (timeout-minutes: 8); :1359-1369 ('ever' implemented as OPEN-only)
findings.fix: Write an intent record BEFORE routing (status PENDING, occ + limit + strategy), then flip it to OPEN after the fill response — so a crash or a job timeout leaves a claim the next cycle can reconcile against broker positions instead of an orphan. Replace the bare `except Exception: continue` at :2539 with a handler that prints the exception and fires _notify when the exception occurred after submission (track a submitted flag on the record), because a silently swallowed live order is exactly the class BREAKDOWNS.md exists for. Measure a six-strategy cycle's wall time against the 8-minute job timeout before shipping, and cut the attempt budget or move the trigger repricing quote earlier (before collect_metadata) if it does not fit. Finally, change the occ guard to scan ALL records, not just OPEN, for the trigger path, so 'ever' means ever.

findings.title: The archive row is not "buy the trigger contract at the ask" — it is a trade-bar close ~90 minutes later, with in-bar look-ahead. Buying at the live ask cannot reproduce it.
findings.attack: The design's whole premise (§ "The defect", lines 9-13) is that the archive corpus "is the return of buying THE CONTRACT THAT PRINTED", so making the live book buy that contract restores comparability. The corpus does not measure that. Entry basis in all three builders is the CLOSE of the first hourly bar that OPENS after the print: probe_tuner.py:123-128 (`today_after` = bars with ts[11:19] > print ts; `e = today_after[0][2]`), glide_sim.py:103-107, grand_retest.py:130-133 (its own comment calls this "what the live engine really does" — grand_retest.py:3-4 — which is false). Alpaca bar `t` is the bar OPEN, so a print at 10:05 selects the 11:00 bar and enters at its 12:00 close: mean latency ~90 minutes, max ~2 hours after the signal. The live path enters at the alert ask within the cycle (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:445, 452-453; repriced to the live ask at 1353-1354). These are different instruments in time as well as in price. Second defect, same lines: those bars are Alpaca OPRA TRADE aggregates (hourly_library.py:40, `/v1beta1/options/bars`), so `e` is a last-sale print, not an executable ask — a direct violation of the house rule that entries are executable-price-only, entry_ref = ask at signal, never mid. Third: the entry bar is ALSO fed to the peak/trail logic (`replay_true(today_after, ...)`, probe_tuner.py:134 and its loop at :59-62), so the trail can arm and the peak can be set on a high that occurred BEFORE the entry close — look-ahead inside the entry bar, and it biases in one direction only (earlier arming, higher floor, better exit on the next session). Fourth: exits fill at synthetic levels — `return fl` where fl = peak*(1-give), and `return stop` exactly (probe_tuner.py:71-73) — never at a bid, never with gap-through. The killer is that the correct input is already banked and unused: uw_flow_prints.py:96-101 stores per-print `executed_at` AND `nbbo_ask`/`nbbo_bid` at execution, and its own docstring (uw_flow_prints.py:3-6) says the point was "entry at the TRUE trigger time and TRUE ask, not the day's closing quote." Every consumer takes only `min(executed_at)` and throws the ask away (probe_tuner.py:90, glide_sim.py:77, grand_retest.py:100, mild_conf_liveband.py:89, mild_conf_split.py:89). Ship the design as drafted and the live book buys the right OCC at the wrong price on the wrong clock, then gets scored against a number built from a later trade print with look-ahead — evidence transfer fails on the price axis while everyone believes it was fixed on the identity axis. capture_ratio.py:136-138 already concedes exactly this in a caveat nobody propagated into the design.
findings.fix: Do not ship the entry-path change until the corpus is rebuilt on the executable basis. (1) Set `e = flow_prints.nbbo_ask` at `min(executed_at)` for that (occ, day), not `today_after[0][2]`; drop the contract when the print carries no ask rather than falling back to the daily quote. (2) Drop the entry bar from the peak/trail loop — pass `today_after[1:]` for peak-tracking, or truncate ta[0] — so nothing arms on a high that preceded entry. (3) Haircut exits to the bid side: the trail/stop fill is a sale, so subtract the cohort's median half-spread (bounded by the 2% cap already enforced) from `fl` and from `stop`, and let a gap-through fill at the bar low, not at the level. (4) Re-publish every cell for the six named strategies on that basis, and mark the current published numbers superseded in the same commit. Only after step 4 does "buy the trigger contract at the live ask" have a comparator. Acceptance: a one-line diff of old vs new day-mean per strategy in the tuner report; if the gap exceeds the promotion floor (+3%/day) the old numbers were never a bar.

findings.title: Affordability is a 3.6x non-monotone conditioner, already measured in-repo, and the proposed ask<=$10 comparator blends a dead slice with a hot one whose own cell was never capped
findings.attack: §4 treats the affordability cut as a bookkeeping correction that "may move the headline numbers". It does not move them; it decides them, and the repo already has the measurement. On the exact DIP_CONF_MILD cell: fullband (any ask) +11.2%/day t+2.63, n=3098/55d; liveband (ask $0.30-4.00, prem 50-400k) +3.1%/day t+0.50, n=290/52d, halves +14/-8 — and on the wide exit the affordable slice is NEGATIVE, -8.8%/day t-1.13 (reports/research/mild_conf_liveband_2026-09-01.md, generated by scripts/mild_conf_liveband.py:94-95). So the affordable-cheap slice is ~9% of the cohort and loses 72% of the day-mean and all of the significance. But it is not monotone: mild_conf_split.py:94-97 shows `inband_expensive` at +21.2%/day t+4.31, n=1337 — nearly double fullband. That $4-9 cell is the precedent this entire design generalizes from (cited verbatim at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2502-2504), and its band is `("inband_expensive", 50000, 400000, 4.00, 1e9)` — ask $4 to INFINITY, no cap. The live gate caps at $9.90 (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1349). Nobody has ever measured the ask<=$10 slice; the nearest count says ask>=$4 is 1337 of 1627 in-band contracts (82%), so the $9.90 ceiling may remove most of the very population that produced +21.2, and the design proposes to adopt it sight-unseen. A single ask<=$10 comparator would average a slice measuring +3.1 (t0.50) with a slice measuring +21.2 (t4.31) and publish a number describing neither — and the live book's actual position in that blend is set by `sorted(..., key=total_premium, reverse=True)[:14]` (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1903), a selection rule the archive comparator does not apply. Worse, the affordable cells are unstable as the corpus grows: BULL_DIP pricey_4_9 -50/80/0.20 across four committed tuner reports runs +20.1% t3.75 (09-04, 112d) → +16.0% t3.15 (09-05) → +11.5% t2.66 (09-07, 152d), a 43% decay in three days; CONSENSUS_CALLS' pricey_4_9 cell was +28.0% t4.67 on 09-01 and had fallen out of the top-10 entirely by 09-07 (fullband +7.1% t5.42 leads). `base_cheap` and `tight_mid` never once appear in any top-10 in any committed tuner report. Two multiple-testing surfaces compound this: probe_tuner.py:156-163 searches 6 buy-variants x 8 exits = 48 cells per strategy and reports the top 10 by t, and mild_conf_split.py searched 4 ask/premium bands on one cell — the $4-9 winner is a survivor of a band search, not a pre-registered constraint. Finally there is a variable mismatch that makes the proposed comparator select the wrong contracts anyway: `r["ask"]` is `contracts_daily.nbbo_ask`, a DAY-level snapshot (probe_tuner.py:104-107,136-138; mild_conf_liveband.py:105), while the live pool gates on the ALERT ask at the print (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1832,1843) and re-gates on a live indicative quote at cycle time (1349). Restricting the archive on the daily ask does not reproduce the live admission set. And the exits are still wrong even after the entry is fixed: scripts/tuner_apply.py:36-38 pins INCUMBENT_POOL = FOLLOW_CALLS→fullband, CONSENSUS_CALLS→fullband, BULL_DIP→base_cheap, DIP_CONVEXITY→base_cheap — so post-change these strategies would BUY from ask<=$10 while the Friday glide keeps tuning their stop/trail on a price-unrestricted cohort. The instrument mismatch moves from the entry to the exit config; the design's Coverage section (lines 43-48) never mentions tuner_apply.py.
findings.fix: Make the affordability constraint part of the STRATEGY DEFINITION, not a post-hoc comparator patch, and pre-register the band before re-deriving anything. (1) Publish the three-way split for every one of the six strategies on the rebuilt executable corpus: ask<=$4, $4<ask<=$9.90, ask>$9.90 — with n, days, day-mean, t, both halves, episode-drop. Pre-register that the live band is $4.00-$9.90 (what sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1349 actually enforces) BEFORE looking, so the band is not re-selected on the answer. (2) Use `flow_prints.nbbo_ask` at the trigger print for the cut, not `contracts_daily.nbbo_ask`, so the archive admission set matches the live one. (3) If a strategy's $4-$9.90 cell does not independently clear the existing bar (n>=150, both halves>0, episode-drop>0), it is not eligible for the trigger path at all — mark it not-live-comparable and leave it synthesizing, rather than shipping an entry change whose comparator does not exist. (4) In the same commit, retarget scripts/tuner_apply.py:36-38 INCUMBENT_POOL to the affordable band for every strategy moved onto the trigger path, or the exits stay mismatched. (5) Given the +20.1→+11.5 decay in three days of corpus growth, add a stability gate: the band's day-mean must not have moved more than one promotion-floor (3 points) across the last three corpus refreshes, or it is noise being sampled, not an edge being measured.

findings.title: Option (b) is a verdict-laundering surface: the court has no reader for occ_source, no multiplicity control, endogenous stream assignment — and no clock that a code-only entry change can restart
findings.attack: Ruling on the panel's question: (b) as drafted is not a legitimate separation. Four counts, all in scripts/sunday_boundary.py. (i) NO READER. The probe court buckets purely by name — `st_ = r.get("probe_strategy")` at :325, then `by_strat.setdefault(st_, {}).setdefault(day, [])` at :336. `occ_source` is written in five places in sandbox_proactive_lab.py (1202, 1207, 1209, 1218, 1317) and read by exactly two assertions in scripts/regime_drill.py:80,99 — nothing in the scorer, nothing in the gate. So ship (b) with the design's stated Coverage (MOT fixtures + one regime-drill scenario per branch, lines 43-48) and the two streams silently POOL into one verdict under one name: a tag with no reader, which is the fail-open-and-quiet category the charter calls the primary enemy. (ii) NO MULTIPLICITY CONTROL. If it is actually implemented, six strategies x two streams = twelve independent draws at the same bar — `t >= 1.8` one-sided (~5.5%) plus floor plus both-halves (:398-400) — re-evaluated EVERY Sunday on a rolling window, against one shared control. There is no correction anywhere in the file. Splitting a strategy in two does not halve its evidence requirement; it doubles its chances to clear a fixed bar, and the strategy keeps its name in whichever stream wins. That is the definition of laundering. (iii) ENDOGENOUS ASSIGNMENT. A fill lands in the trigger stream only if `_TRIG_CANDS` held a live-repriceable identity for that ticker in that cycle — which requires the alert spread <=2%, a live quote, and the live ask still inside band (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1349, fail-closed). Those conditions are correlated with liquidity and with the sign of post-print drift, so the split is not a randomisation: the trigger stream is a liquidity-selected subsample and the synth stream is its complement. Comparing either to the same unselected EXEC_BASELINE control estimates nothing about the strategy. (iv) THE CLOCK DOES NOT RESTART. §5 asserts "their virgin-day evidence restarts". Nothing implements that. Probe-level exclusion comes only from `probe.tuning.<name>.applied` (:363-368), written by the Friday exit applier; the blanket/per-key clocks come only from `auto_*` markers in fade_book_spec.json (:278-296), written by the auto-appliers. This change is a code-only edit to sandbox_proactive_lab.py: it writes neither marker, so pre-change synthesized-instrument days keep counting toward the 8-day bar and into the t-test — two instruments inside one verdict, the exact anti-cube violation the file's own comment at :268-271 was written to prevent. The design's "none has 8 closed days, so nothing is lost" is a claim about today's counts, not a mechanism, and it will be false the moment a strategy accrues days on both sides of the commit.
findings.fix: Reject (b) as drafted. Ship the version that preserves throughput without creating a second bar: fallback fills are ALLOWED but DISQUALIFIED from the court — one promotable stream, trigger-only. Concretely: (1) in scripts/sunday_boundary.py:325-336, filter `by_strat` to records whose entered leg carries `occ_source == "uw_trigger_verbatim"` for any strategy on the trigger path; synthesized fills are logged as throughput telemetry and reported in the Sunday lines as "N non-evidence fills", never scored, never promotable. This is (a)'s evidence hygiene at (b)'s throughput. (2) If the owner still wants two scored streams, they are two pre-registered names with two priority slots, a Bonferroni-corrected bar (t>=2.4 at six strategies x two streams), and a written statement that the trigger stream is a liquidity-selected subsample — but I would not sign that, because (iii) means neither stream estimates the strategy. (3) Independently of (a)/(b): add an explicit entry-path clock. Write `probe.entry_path.<name>.changed = <ISO date>` into fade_book_spec.json in the SAME commit as the code change, and extend the exclusion at sunday_boundary.py:363-368 to take `max(tuning.applied, entry_path.changed)`. Without this the clock claim in §5 is decorative. Acceptance: an MOT fixture that appends one pre-change synthesized day and one post-change trigger day and asserts the court counts exactly one.

findings.title: The live repricing gate is an adverse-selection filter with no archive counterpart: it rejects exactly the contracts whose favourable drift has already begun
findings.attack: Answering the design's open question 3 ("what fraction of trigger candidates will die at the repricing gate, and does that reintroduce a selection difference?"). It is worse than a fraction — the deaths are systematically signed. sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1349 fail-closes unless, at cycle time, a live quote exists AND the spread is <=2% AND `_blo <= _la <= 9.9`. A trigger contract admitted to `_TRIG_CANDS` at an alert ask of, say, $8.50 (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1828 admits $4.00-$9.00) is REJECTED if it has run to $10.20 by the time the cycle reaches it — i.e. the engine discards precisely the names where the post-print move the strategy is betting on has already started. Symmetrically a $4.20 contract that decayed to $3.80 is rejected by the same floor. The archive cohort has no analogue of either cut: its entry is a post-print bar CLOSE (probe_tuner.py:128), so it books those run-ups in full and counts them in the day-mean. The result is a live distribution whose right tail is truncated by construction against a comparator that includes it — and in a cohort whose returns are this skewed, the right tail IS the mean. This is not the friction the capture ratio was built to expose; it is a censoring rule, and it will read as "the edge didn't survive contact" while the real cause is that the engine refused the winners. Two aggravating details: the gate prices off `feed=indicative` (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1339-1340), a synthesized quote rather than executable OPRA NBBO, so entry_ref honesty is asserted against a non-executable number; and the band boundary is asymmetric — the pool admits <=$9.00 (1828) but the gate admits <=$9.90 (1349), while the design proposes $10, three different ceilings for one constraint.
findings.fix: (1) Instrument the gate before shipping: log every `trigger_contract fail-closed` skip with the alert ask, the live ask, and the reason, and after two weeks publish the drift distribution of rejects. If rejects are systematically higher than their alert ask, the gate is censoring winners and the comparator must be censored identically. (2) Mirror the censoring into the archive: the re-derived comparator must drop any archive contract whose price at `today_after[0]` (the archive's own entry point, or the rebuilt ask basis) sits outside the same $4.00-$9.90 window — that reproduces the live admission rule instead of pretending it does not exist. Without this step the ask<=$10 comparator of §4 is still not live-comparable. (3) Collapse the three ceilings to one constant read from fade_book_spec.json, so pool (1828), gate (1349) and comparator cannot drift apart again. (4) Add an MOT fixture asserting a candidate admitted at $8.50 and repriced to $10.20 is skipped with a distinguishable reason code, so the reject class is countable rather than lumped into generic skips.

findings.title: EXEC_BASELINE cannot be the control that isolates instrument identity — it has the identical mismatch, and the gap it "captures" by is a tenth of the study's own declared noise floor
findings.attack: The design's causal claim (lines 15-17) is: EXEC_BASELINE captures (live median +5.70 vs archive +4.67, gap +1.03), therefore "Execution friction is not the problem; instrument identity is." That inference does not hold on either leg. First, EXEC_BASELINE buys SYNTHESIZED contracts exactly like the strategies it is being contrasted with: its pool is the `else` branch `candidates[2:12]` (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2501), which carries no `occ`, so `build_legs` falls through the `_PROBE_CONTRACT` early-return (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:443-455) into the 4%-OTM/35-DTE synthesis path (:475-497). Its archive comparator is `("EXEC_BASELINE", lambda r: True, BASE)` over `glide_fine_rows.jsonl` (scripts/capture_ratio.py:34,51-58) — the same per-OCC trigger corpus, entered at the same post-print bar close. So EXEC_BASELINE has the SAME synthesized-vs-trigger mismatch and captures anyway. Either instrument identity is not what breaks capture, or EXEC_BASELINE's capture is as uninterpretable as everyone else's — the design cannot have it both ways, and it is currently using the second case as proof of the first. The control that would actually isolate instrument identity does not exist yet: it would be the same strategy predicate run on trigger fills and on synthesized fills over shared days, which is the thing option (b) claims to build and cannot (see the court finding). Second, the magnitude is inadmissible on its own terms. scripts/capture_ratio.py:126-130 states in its own output that "with this many days and option returns this skewed, no gap smaller than roughly 10 points is distinguishable from noise - this study is a measurement instrument that is not yet loaded, and its own honest output today is 'not enough closed evidence'." The design cites a +1.03 gap — one tenth of that floor — as corroboration. It also cites it as a median-vs-median comparison while the script's own row (:110-111) reports THIN for anything under 5 shared days and the weighted line excludes THIN rows entirely (:112-115); the design does not say how many shared days EXEC_BASELINE had. And the report it cites, reports/research/capture_ratio_2026-09-09.md, does not exist in the repo — only the generator does — so the number is unverifiable from the tree. Building a six-strategy entry-path change on it is acting on a reading the instrument disclaims.
findings.fix: Strike the EXEC_BASELINE corroboration from the design, or replace it with a control that can carry the claim. (1) Commit the capture_ratio output the design cites, with its shared-day counts and THIN flags visible; a design premise that cannot be checked against a committed artefact is not a premise. findings.title: Trigger-only (option a) starves these six to near-zero: the pool head collapses 16 -> 3-9 names, and the engine's ONE existing trigger-identity pool has an observed conversion of 1 fill in ~76
findings.attack:
MEASURED, not argued. I replayed the exact proposed filter chain over the three real whole-market UW flow_alerts snapshots on disk that carry NBBO (data/cache_uw: 2026-06-02 n=500, 2026-06-08 n=500, 2026-07-01 n=300; the 200-row caches have null bid/ask and are unusable). Funnel per snapshot -> non-index -> calls -> premium 50k-1M -> ask-side aggressor -> spread<=2% -> DTE>=7 -> ask<=$10:
  2026-06-02: 493 -> 310 -> 279 -> 151 -> 58 -> 51 -> 10 rows / 9 tickers
  2026-06-08: 467 -> 266 -> 224 -> 116 -> 38 -> 26 -> 5 rows / 3 tickers
  2026-07-01: 272 -> 161 ->  87 ->  42 -> 13 ->  9 -> 3 rows / 3 tickers
Against the pools these six draw today, same snapshots: _FULL_CANDS = 44 / 27 / 34 tickers, head-capped [:16]. So on 2026-07-01 (the one snapshot pulled at a ~10k premium floor, i.e. the closest analogue to the live 600-row/50k-floor pull at sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1801-1810) the usable head goes 16 -> 3. Caveat stated plainly: the two 500-row snapshots were pulled at min_premium 200-250k, so they over-weight the premium tail and their counts are not a clean scale-up; the 07-01 read is the honest one and it is the worst.

The decisive number is not an extrapolation. _PRICEY_CANDS is ALREADY a trigger-identity pool built from the same filter family (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1828-1850, published at :1902-1903). On the same three snapshots it yields 2 / 1 / 1 tickers per cycle. It feeds DIP_CONF_MILD and BULL_DIP_X (:2499) and, per the design's own occ_source audit, has produced exactly ONE fill out of ~76 PROBE fills. That is the observed conversion rate of trigger-identity entry in this engine, measured on the live book, not modelled.

Then the throttles compound on top of a 3-9 name pool: six strategies share it; within a cycle the first taker removes the ticker for the rest (:2509); the occ-collision guard removes that contract from every book for the life of the position (:1359-1379) and the pool carries at most one occ per ticker; the cycle caps at 2 entries / 10 attempts (:2483); and BULL_DIP / DIP_CONVEXITY / DIP_CONF_MILD are mutually exclusive on spy_regime (:2388, :2395, :2403), so on any given day at most one of the three can even bid, and BULL_DIP additionally needs that ticker below its own 20d SMA. Note the surviving names are QQQ, SPY, NVDA, GOOGL, AAPL, AMZN, TSLA, GLD, XLE, INTC, AA, NOK, IREN - the mega-cap/ETF core where the FADE book already concentrates, so the collision guard bites hardest exactly where the pool is richest.

Design section 5 restarts all six evidence clocks. Trigger-only therefore restarts six 8-day virgin-day clocks onto a path whose measured fill rate is ~1 in 76. Those six will not reach 8 closed days this year, and the proof account cannot seat anyone on strategies that never close a trade. Option (a) is not 'cleanest evidence, costs throughput' - it is no evidence at all.

On the panel's actual question, (b) as drawn is also not shippable: the synthesized stream fires precisely on the cycles and names where no cheap tight-spread call printed, so the two streams are not one strategy measured two ways - they are a liquidity/tape split, the trigger stream sampling only the mega-cap/ETF core and the synthesized stream carrying everything else. With the trigger stream at ~2-5% of the synthesized stream's n, every promotion decision will de facto be made on the synthesized stream while the strategy carries the trigger stream's headline number. That is the laundering surface, and it is structural, not a bookkeeping problem.

findings.fix: Reject (a) outright and do not ship (b) as a fallback branch of six existing strategies. Ship section 4 (comparator honesty) ALONE first: re-derive every published cell for these six on the live-reachable slice, with no entry-path change and no clock restart. That is free, costs zero throughput, and is the only step that can be evaluated on its own merits. If the re-derived cells still show edge, then register the trigger path as ONE new strategy with its own name, its own pool and its own virgin-day clock - not as a mode of six incumbents - so the court compares two named strategies rather than two streams inside one. Before any of that, publish the funnel counts above as a standing per-cycle diagnostic (the scan already logs a starved-cycle line at :2565-2568; add pool sizes to it) so the owner can see the pool before the change, not after.

findings.title: 39% of the design's own pool is dead on arrival: the fail-closed repricing gate defaults band_lo to $4.00, so every _TRIG_CANDS candidate priced under $4 is guaranteed to skip
findings.attack:
The design specifies the pool as ask <= $10 with no floor (instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:22-24). The gate it must pass reads `_blo = _tl.get("band_lo", 4.0)` and then requires `_blo <= _la <= 9.9` (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1347, :1349). The trigger-contract leg built by build_legs' _PROBE_CONTRACT path sets no band_lo key at all (:450-455) - only the afford_fallback path sets one, to 0.30 (:1316). So a _TRIG_CANDS leg inherits 4.00 and any candidate whose live ask is below $4.00 fail-closes on a condition that has nothing to do with the quote being stale, crossed or wide.

Measured on the same 18 survivors: 7 of 18 (39%) price below $4.00 - asks 1.11, 1.40, 2.99, 3.10, 3.57, 3.75, 3.75. Per snapshot the pool goes 10 -> 5, 5 -> 5, 3 -> 1 usable names. The 07-01 snapshot, the live-like one, drops to a SINGLE candidate for the entire roster. The ceiling is wrong too: the gate caps at 9.90, the design says $10, so a 9.95 candidate is admitted to the pool and then skipped (no survivor hit this in my sample, but the constant mismatch is real).

This is not a tuning question, it is a silent contradiction between two constants that live 500 lines apart, and the design document never mentions band_lo. It will present as unexplained starvation - the same symptom the owner has been chasing all week - and the skip reason string at :1351 says 'ask outside 4.0-9.9', which reads like a data problem rather than a config collision. Worse, this failure mode is invisible to the proposed MOT coverage: section 6 lists filter unit checks on the POOL (band, aggressor, spread, DTE, ask cap) and a trigger-path fixture asserting the entered OCC, but a fixture built with a $5 candidate passes while every sub-$4 candidate dies in production.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:1347 (`_blo = _tl.get("band_lo", 4.0)`); :1349 (`... and _blo <= _la <= 9.9`); :1350-1351 (skip + misleading reason string); :443-455 (build_legs trigger path sets no band_lo); :1316 (afford_fallback sets band_lo 0.30, proving the key is the intended lever); :1828 (existing pricey pool's 4.00 < pc <= 9.00 source of the 4.0 default); reports/instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:22-24 (pool spec says ask <= $10, no floor)
findings.fix: Define the band once, as a single module-level constant pair (e.g. TRIG_ASK_LO / TRIG_ASK_HI), and have scan_candidates' _TRIG_CANDS filter, build_legs' leg construction (setting band_lo explicitly) and the repricing check at :1349 all read it. Make the MOT fixture parametric over the band edges - a candidate at LO, at LO-0.01, at HI, at HI+0.01 - so a future edit to either end fails a test instead of silently starving the book. Separately, split the skip reason so 'no live quote', 'crossed', 'spread>2%' and 'outside band' are distinct codes; they are being aggregated into one string at :1351 and that is why this class of starvation is hard to see in the logs.

findings.title: The archive corpus has NO DTE floor and NO ask cap - so 'the SAME filters the archive corpus used' is false, and the ask cap selects contracts 6x further out of the money, changing the hypothesis rather than the instrument
findings.attack:
The design's premise is that _TRIG_CANDS reproduces the archive's own filters (instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:20-24). Read the corpus builder: probe_tuner.py:103-108 selects on total_premium 50k-1M, ask_volume > bid_volume, and NBBO present - nothing else. Line 116-117 adds spread <= 2% computed on MID. There is no expiry predicate anywhere in build_rows, and no ask-price predicate; ask is merely STORED (:136-138) so BUY_VARIANTS can slice on it later (:156-163). WINNER_PROFILE's cells are worse: winner_profile_sim.py:97-98 filters only on premium floor and IV ceiling - no side, no DTE, no ask. So DTE>=7 and ask<=$10 are live-only cuts that the published cells never carried.

How much do they cut? On the three snapshots, the archive-eligible cohort (calls + 50k-1M + aggressor + spread<=2%) is n=109. Only 18 survive both live cuts - 16%. The published numbers describe a cohort of which the live book can reach one contract in six.

And the survivors are not a random sixth. Measured geometry, survivors vs dropped:
  survivors (n=18): median moneyness +12.4% OTM, median DTE 45, median ask/underlying 2.41%
  dropped   (n=91): median moneyness  +2.0% OTM, median DTE 45, median ask/underlying 5.65%
Identical median DTE. The ask cap does not buy a nearer expiry - it buys a strike SIX TIMES further out of the money on the same clock. The design's open question 2 guesses 'further OTM or nearer expiry'; the answer is unambiguously the first, and that is the worse of the two, because it is a delta shift, not a horizon shift. FOLLOW_CALLS' +15.9%/day was earned on a cohort whose median contract sat ~2% OTM at 45 DTE - roughly a 0.45-0.55 delta instrument. The live book would buy ~0.15-0.25 delta lottery tickets. Those are not the same bet: far higher probability of total loss, far fatter right tail, and a completely different sensitivity of option return to underlying return.

That last point breaks the exit grid too. The exits (-50/+50/0.20 baseline, -70/+80/0.30 wide) were selected by replaying the ~ATM cohort (probe_tuner.py:32-33, :133-135). On a 12%-OTM contract a -50% option move is a far smaller underlying move than on a 2%-OTM contract, so the stop fires much more often and the +50% trail-trigger arms on much smaller moves. Every exit cell in the tuner is being applied to an instrument whose return distribution it was never fitted on.

Conclusion the panel needs: section 4 (comparator honesty) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. Re-deriving cells on the affordable slice fixes the number; it does not fix that the tuner never searched exits on that slice, and it does not fix that a 12%-OTM strategy is a different registered hypothesis from a 2%-OTM one. The design's own alternative in open question 2 - 'does the strategy definition itself need the constraint' - is the correct answer, and it is a yes.

findings.fix: Add ask<=10 and DTE>=7 as an explicit BUY_VARIANT pair in probe_tuner.py's grid and re-run the full strategy x variant x exit cube on that slice before any of the six is re-registered. Report the cell counts - if n falls under the existing PASS bar of 150 (probe_tuner.py:216) then the honest verdict is 'this strategy has no evidence on the instrument we can buy', which is a legitimate and cheap outcome. Publish the moneyness distribution of the affordable slice alongside every re-derived cell so the delta shift is visible in the report rather than buried. And amend the design text: strike 'the SAME filters the archive corpus used' - it is the single sentence the whole build rests on and it is not true.

findings.title: The build's corroborating evidence is ten times below its own stated noise floor, and the report it comes from does not exist in the repo
findings.attack:
The design justifies spending throughput with one empirical claim: 'EXEC_BASELINE - whose archive comparator is the unfiltered pool and which makes no instrument claim - CAPTURES (live median +5.70 vs archive +4.67, gap +1.03). Execution friction is not the problem; instrument identity is' (instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:15-18). That inference is the load-bearing beam: it is what licenses ruling out friction and paying for instrument identity with fills.

The instrument that produced it disagrees with it in writing. scripts/capture_ratio.py:126-130 ends its own READING block with: 'POWER WARNING: with this many days and option returns this skewed, no gap smaller than roughly 10 points is distinguishable from noise - this study is a measurement instrument that is not yet loaded, and its own honest output today is not enough closed evidence.' The design's +1.03 gap is a tenth of that floor. The script also flags any row under 5 shared days as THIN and says such rows 'must not be quoted as a verdict' (:15-16, :109). The design quotes one as a verdict.

Separately: reports/research/capture_ratio_2026-09-09.md does not exist in this repo - I was asked to read it and it is absent. The script cannot produce it here either: it opens reports/research/glide_fine_rows.jsonl unguarded at :51 and that corpus file is not in the tree. So the number cannot be reproduced or checked from what is committed.

The throughput consequence is direct. The owner is being asked to trade measured fills - the pool head from 16 to 3-9 names, on a mechanism whose observed conversion is 1 in 76 - for a defect whose 'it isn't friction' half rests on a reading its author declared un-loaded. If friction is in fact still material, the instrument change costs the throughput AND leaves the gap. The two hypotheses have not been separated; one of them was dismissed on a +1.03.
findings.evidence: scripts/capture_ratio.py:126-130 (the ~10-point noise floor and the 'not yet loaded' self-assessment); :15-16 and :109 (THIN rule, never a verdict); :51 (unguarded read of reports/research/glide_fine_rows.jsonl, which is absent from the repo); :131-134 (the script's own no-overlap branch: 'the gate's capture requirement cannot be met until closed live evidence accumulates'); reports/instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:15-18 (the claim); reports/research/capture_ratio_2026-09-09.md (does not exist)
findings.fix: Either strike lines 15-18 from the design and state honestly that friction has not been ruled out, or hold the entry-path change until capture_ratio has non-THIN rows and a gap that clears its own stated floor. Commit the generated capture_ratio_2026-09-09.md (or state in the design that the corpus lives only on the VPS and cite the run id) so the panel can check the number. Guard capture_ratio.py:51 so a missing corpus prints 'corpus unavailable' rather than raising - a study that silently cannot run is worse than one that reports nothing. Note this does not weaken the PRIMARY evidence, which is sound: the occ_source audit showing 1 of ~76 fills bought the trigger contract is a direct observation and needs no capture ratio to stand.

findings.title: WINNER_PROFILE and WINNER_PROFILE_X are both-sides, regime-agnostic strategies; routing them through a calls-only trigger pool deletes half their hypothesis and collapses the control/variant pair into two identical predicates
findings.attack:
The design moves WINNER_PROFILE and WINNER_PROFILE_X onto _TRIG_CANDS, which is calls-only by spec (instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:21-27). Neither strategy has ever been a calls strategy. Their live predicates carry no side condition (sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2413-2415, :2424), they are deliberately excluded from the _CALLS_ONLY set that gates the other six (:2470-2471), and the roster comment states the design intent outright: 'Regime-agnostic, both sides' (:2421). The archive cells that produced the numbers agree - winner_profile_sim.py:97-98 selects on premium floor and IV ceiling only, so puts are in the +6.33%/day cohort by construction.

So this is not the instrument fix the document describes. For these two, moving to _TRIG_CANDS silently removes the put half of the population, and then section 5 restarts their evidence clocks - meaning a fresh 8-day clock starts on a strategy that is no longer the one that was registered, judged against archive cells that still include puts. That is precisely the failure the whole document exists to correct, reintroduced in the same change.

Second problem, measured: the two are supposed to be a frozen control (premium > 73,200) versus a best-variables variant (premium > 100,000) - see the roster comments at :2416-2429. On _TRIG_CANDS the field they test changes meaning as well as magnitude: today `total_premium` on a _FULL_CANDS row is the TICKER AGGREGATE summed across every alert for that name (:1881-1889), whereas on a trigger-identity row it is the PER-ALERT premium of one contract (:1846). Both thresholds are already no-ops in both worlds - on my snapshots 16 of 16 _FULL_CANDS head members clear both, and 18 of 18 _TRIG_CANDS survivors clear both (per-alert medians $355k and $359k, against a pool floored at 50k). So the pair is already degenerate, and on a 3-9 name shared pool it becomes actively harmful: two identical predicates racing for the same handful of tickers, where the first to enter removes the name for the other (:2509) and its contract for every book (:1359-1379). The 'control vs best-variables' comparison the roster promises cannot be run on that pool.

The same question the document raises about BULL_DIP and DIP_CONVEXITY (open question 4 - their live filters are md-level and the trigger pool does not carry them) applies with more force here, because for WP/WP_X the mismatch is in the hypothesis itself, not just the filter plumbing.
findings.evidence: sandbox_proactive_lab.py:2413-2415 (WINNER_PROFILE: premium + IV, no side); :2416-2423 (comment: 'Regime-agnostic, both sides', 'teacher freeze; rebuild only by owner order'); :2424-2429 (WINNER_PROFILE_X: premium only); :2470-2471 (_CALLS_ONLY deliberately excludes both); :1881-1889 (_FULL_CANDS total_premium is the ticker aggregate); :1846 (aggx total_premium is per-alert); :2509-2510 and :1359-1379 (shared-pool contention); scripts/winner_profile_sim.py:97-98 (archive cells carry no side filter); reports/instrument_mismatch_design_2026-09-09.md:26-27 (the six named), :58-60 (the analogous open question for BULL_DIP / DIP_CONVEXITY)
findings.fix: Drop WINNER_PROFILE and WINNER_PROFILE_X from this change. Their instrument mismatch is real but the remedy is a both-sides trigger pool (admit puts, keep the aggressor test side-correct: ask_vol > bid_vol on the printed side), not the calls-only pool built for FOLLOW_CALLS. If the panel wants them in scope now, the honest route is to close them as REJECTED in ROADMAP.md and re-register the calls-only trigger versions under new names with fresh clocks, so nothing inherits a number measured on a different population. Independently of this change, resolve the degenerate pair: with both thresholds clearing 100% of both pools, WINNER_PROFILE and WINNER_PROFILE_X are testing the same thing and one of them is dead weight (Adversarial Architect check 5) - either re-floor WINNER_PROFILE_X onto a premium that actually bites the per-alert distribution, or retire it. And rename the field: a `total_premium` key that means ticker-aggregate on one pool and per-alert on another will produce a wrong threshold the first time someone reuses it.
